outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Chips & AI hardware, led by AMD, TSM and Broadcom
strongest.reason: AI-chip demand stayed resilient even as the broader market sold off, with TSMC's advanced-packaging capacity for AI chips reportedly sold out through 2026 and continued fund rotation into foundry and accelerator leaders

strongest.area: AI infrastructure & cloud, led by Oracle
strongest.reason: Oracle extended its rally into Thursday's earnings on the strength of its $300B OpenAI cloud deal, positioning it as a key proxy for continued hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending

weakest.area: Enterprise software, led by ServiceNow and Cadence/Synopsys
weakest.reason: ServiceNow dropped sharply in broad risk-off selling tied to the Strait of Hormuz escalation given its demanding valuation, while the EDA design-software pair extended a multi-day slide on rising yields

weakest.area: Robotics-adjacent names, led by Intuitive Surgical
weakest.reason: shares remain in a multi-decade valuation reset following JNJ's FDA-authorized Ottava entry into soft-tissue robotic surgery, a direct challenge to Intuitive's roughly 80% market share

outlook.nextStep: The escalating US-Iran tanker conflict in the Strait of Hormuz is the dominant new risk worth tracking closely, given its direct line to oil prices, yields and the Sept 15-16 Fed decision; Wednesday and Thursday's back-to-back Adobe and Oracle earnings are also worth watching given the double-digit-percent swings options markets are pricing in. Day-to-day chip-stock moves and ServiceNow's geopolitics-driven drop are probably better watched than acted on until the picture clarifies.

signals.title: US-Iran tanker conflict in the Strait of Hormuz escalates
signals.body: US forces struck and disabled several Iranian oil tankers after Iran's IRGC fired ballistic missiles toward a US carrier group; Iran has separately targeted tankers and floated a maritime 'exclusion zone' near the strait. Brent crude briefly topped $100/barrel and WTI pushed above $94 on the escalation.
signals.focus: the single biggest swing factor in markets right now, worth tracking closely for further escalation or de-escalation

signals.title: 10-year yield nears 4.8% as Fed rate call stays contested
signals.body: The 10-year Treasury yield pushed toward 4.81%, its highest since October 2023, as the oil-driven inflation scare added weight to the case for a hike at the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting. Fed Governor Waller has said his decision hinges heavily on next week's August CPI report, while the Trump administration is pushing for a hold or cut.
signals.focus: the most important economic date this month worth tracking closely; day-to-day comment-driven swings are probably better watched than traded on

signals.title: ServiceNow drops sharply on geopolitical risk-off selling
signals.body: ServiceNow fell over 7% in broad risk-off selling tied to the Strait of Hormuz escalation, a move amplified by a valuation above 85x earnings that leaves it especially exposed to macro-driven reversals.
signals.focus: a valuation-driven amplification of a macro shock worth watching for stabilization rather than a reason to chase the dip

signals.title: Adobe and Oracle earnings loom with double-digit implied swings
signals.body: Adobe reports Q3 results Thursday with options pricing an 8% potential move, amid a pending CEO transition (Anil Chakravarthy succeeds Shantanu Narayen in December) and split analyst opinion on AI-disruption risk to Creative Cloud. Oracle reports fiscal Q1 results the same week with an even larger ~11% implied swing, given scrutiny of what its AI cloud capex is delivering.
signals.focus: two binary, high-implied-volatility events worth watching resolve rather than positioning around ahead of time

signals.title: TSMC's AI chip packaging capacity reportedly sold out through 2026
signals.body: TSMC's advanced packaging capacity for AI chips is described as extremely tight and sold out through 2026, reinforcing resilient demand for foundry leaders even as the broader semiconductor index has pulled back roughly 9.5% from a month earlier on profit-taking.
signals.focus: a supportive supply-demand data point worth noting, though the broader chip pullback suggests some of the good news is already known

signals.title: JNJ's Ottava robot begins challenging Intuitive Surgical's dominance
signals.body: Johnson & Johnson has received FDA De Novo authorization for its Ottava soft-tissue robotic surgery platform, marking its formal entry into a market Intuitive Surgical has controlled with roughly 80% share for over two decades. Intuitive shares are described as trading near a decade-low valuation amid the competitive overhang, even as its newer Ion platform shows 36% procedure growth.
signals.focus: a structural, multi-quarter competitive story worth a closer look rather than a one-day headline to react to

signals.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows fall sharply entering holiday period
signals.body: Spot Bitcoin ETF inflows fell roughly 76% heading into the recent Labor Day break, with only BlackRock and Fidelity still attracting meaningful fresh money, as Bitcoin and Ethereum both cooled from August's stronger pace.
signals.focus: a demand-side cooling signal worth tracking over the next few weeks rather than reacting to on a single soft data point
